suggestions.rationale: Persistent post-traumatic headache is a recognized post-concussive condition, but it is a distinct diagnosis from primary migraine even when the clinical phenotype is migraine-like. Current reviews support phenotype-guided management after concussion and mild traumatic brain injury. Because this catalog target is `migraine-headaches`, the relationship is limited to cases in which a clinician has diagnosed migraine or persistent post-traumatic headache with a migraine/probable-migraine phenotype and documented the temporal relationship to the concussion. The evidence does not justify relabeling every persistent post-concussion headache as migraine or inferring an individual nexus from symptom overlap alone.
evidenceGaps: Headache-specialist or neurology diagnosis distinguishing persistent post-traumatic headache from primary migraine and documenting any migraine phenotype
Concussion and headache chronology, including onset and persistence after the qualifying injury
Pre-injury migraine/headache history and other competing headache causes
Headache phenotype, frequency, associated features, disability, and treatment response
Qualified clinician assessment addressing the individual's diagnostic relationship to the documented concussion

sourceReferences.citation: Gallivan LMA, Kacperski J. Current Research on the Diagnosis and Management of Persistent Post-Traumatic Headache. Curr Pain Headache Rep. 2026;30(1):67. PMID 42133249
sourceReferences.note: Clinical review describes persistent post-traumatic headache after concussion/mild TBI and supports phenotype-guided management while noting limited evidence. Supports bounded post-concussion headache research, not automatic reclassification as migraine.
